newsitem.title: UK: Med Aframax tanker rates firm, NWE fuel rates dip.
newsitem.headline: Med Aframax tanker rates firm, NWE fuel rates dip.

text.p: Crude oil tanker rates for 80,000 tonne Aframax tankers were steady to firmer for cross-Med voyages on Thursday while smaller fuel oil vessel owners were expected to ask lower numbers, shipping brokers said.

While NOC's fixture of the 78,000 tonne Athenian Faith from Zueitina to Sarroch at W125 was seen well above market because of the premium attached to the Libyan portion of the voyage, the market for standard cross-Med voyages was pegged around W107.50.
Fuel oil supply from the Baltics appeared drying up. Rates were hard to assess due a lack of fixing, but one broker said 25,000 tonners were about W200, off some 10 points from Tuesday.
Two Ultra Large Crude Carriers (ULCCs) were fixed from the Mideast to the U.S. Gulf, one at W50 and another at W47.5. These prices were roughly in line with earlier ULCC fixtures.

Rates for voyages in the Western Hemisphere were hard to assess because of the holiday in the U.S. A late scramble to fix vessels on Wednesday resulted in fixtures of 70,000 tonne vessels for Caribbean/USG routes being done as high as W145.
Transatlantic business from the North Sea was thin because of the U.S. holiday but an arbitrage window appeared to have opened for crude oil barrels from the North Sea to the Med.
The 130,000 tonne Marble was fixed by Total for a journey from Mongstad to Lavera at W95, and crude oil traders said they thought more barrels could move in the same direction.

Inter/UKCont rates for 80,000 tonners were steady or slightly firmer and fixing activity was healthy. The Torinita was chartered at W100 and brokers said they thought this was broadly representative of the market.
